steps.name: Threads sit above tasks on Home
steps.goal: Look at the Home screen list. Do not open anything.
steps.done: A Threads section with the Pricing ideas thread is at the top of the list, and a Tasks section follows it.

steps.name: A thread reads like Slack
steps.goal: Tap the row named Pricing ideas under the Threads heading. Do not tap the message field.
steps.done: The thread is open. Messages from Alex and Demo sit on the left under their names, and omg's answers are not in the main list.
expect: @omg also fix the typo in the signup email
forbid: Linear starts at $8 per seat a month.

steps.name: Replies show the task state
steps.goal: Read the reply links under the messages near the end of the thread. Do not tap anything.
steps.done: The messages that asked omg for work say how many replies they have, one with a task that needs you and one with a task that is done.

steps.name: omg answers in the replies
steps.goal: Tap the reply link that says the task needs you.
steps.done: The Replies page is open (its title is Replies, the thread name under it), scrolled to the end: the newest reply and the task's question are on screen.
expect: Agreed. Ship it after the Stripe question.

steps.name: The reply bar sits above the keyboard
steps.goal: Tap the text field that says Reply… at the bottom of the replies sheet. It must be tapped even if it is already visible, so the keyboard opens. Do not type anything.
steps.done: The on-screen keyboard is open (letter keys are listed) and the Reply… field is still listed above it.

steps.name: Back from the replies
steps.goal: Tap Back at the top left of the Replies page.
steps.done: The replies page is gone and the thread's main list is visible again.

steps.name: A mention is a tag that shows the members
steps.goal: In the thread, tap the highlighted @omg tag at the start of a message (for example in "@omg also fix the typo in the signup email"). Tap the tag itself, not the reply link under the message.
steps.done: The thread details sheet is open, listing the members and omg.
expect: Answers, or starts a task, when someone writes @omg
